title: Recording: That Is All by George Harrison | 1972
content:
Apple Studios, London
Producer: George Harrison
Engineer: Phil McDonald

George Harrison recorded ‘That Is All’, for his fourth solo album Living In The Material World, on 10 October 1972.

Twenty-eight takes had been recorded the previous day, but the song was left unfinished at the end of the session.

The basic track had Klaus Voormann’s bass guitar on track one, and Jim Keltner’s drums on two, three and four. Harrison’s electric guitar was fed through a Leslie revolving speaker and recorded on tracks seven and eight, and his vocals were on 10. Nicky Hopkins alternated between piano, recorded on tracks five and six, and harpsichord on 15 and 16. Gary Wright played a Wurlitzer organ on tracks 11 and 12.

Following take 8 the musicians jammed a version of ‘Tea For Two’. The penultimate take of ‘That Is All’, take 31, was marked as the best, and became the album version.
